overview: This bill changes federal tax and firearms rules for "less-than-lethal" devices, such as launchers that fire pepper or rubber projectiles. It defines such a device as one that can't fire regular gun ammunition, doesn't shoot projectiles faster than 500 feet per second, is designed not to cause death or serious injury, and can't take standard gun magazines. Those devices and their ammunition would be exempt from the federal excise tax (a sales tax paid by makers and importers) on firearms and ammunition, and from the National Firearms Act, a law that requires registration and a tax on certain weapons. The Treasury Department would have to decide within 90 days whether a device qualifies when a manufacturer asks, publish an updated list each year, and report to Congress on devices that fire faster than the limit. As of February 2, 2026, the House Ways and Means Committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say lowering taxes and paperwork on non-lethal options will make them cheaper and easier for police and the public to get, encouraging alternatives to deadly force.
against: Critics say exempting these devices from federal firearms rules reduces oversight of weapons that can still injure people, and relies on Treasury to judge which new products are truly non-lethal.
